plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Cascading chains of fragrant, pea-like flowers drape from twining vines over pergolas, temple walkways and garden arches. Some racemes grow to nearly a metre long and sway in the spring breeze.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late April to mid-May in the temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Japan, where it is celebrated in famous wisteria gardens, and in temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine in a set direction. Japanese wisteria climbs clockwise, while Chinese wisteria climbs counterclockwise.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: Dense, cone-shaped clusters of intensely perfumed blossoms cover this hardy shrub. It is a nostalgic favourite of cottage gardens and old farmsteads.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late April to late May in cool temperate climates of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens across the northeastern United States, southern Canada and northern and central Europe, with wild origins in the Balkans
plants.funFact: Each lilac floret usually has four petals. Finding one with five is traditionally said to bring good luck.

plants.name: Aloe arborescens
plants.description: Tall, branching aloes with blue-green rosettes send up torch-like spikes of flame-coloured tubular flowers. They glow against the winter landscape and attract sunbirds that come to feed on the nectar.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter, roughly May to August in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Coastal and rocky slopes of South Africa, including the Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal
plants.funFact: Krantz aloe flowers in the dry southern winter, when little else is in bloom. That makes it a key nectar source for sunbirds and other pollinators.
